Address-sharing statistics for a reference corpus

Source: R/normalize.R
np_addr_freq.Rd

Counts how many reference records sit at each exact address, at each address

  • suite, and how many distinct suites each address carries. This is what makes a suite match interpretable rather than merely true:

Usage

np_addr_freq(
  street_keys,
  zip5 = NULL,
  unit_ids = NULL,
  name_keys = NULL,
  share_min = 10L,
  unit_coverage_min = 0.5
)

Arguments

street_keys

Normalized street (reference street_key).

zip5

Five-digit ZIP, so one street name in two towns is two addresses.

unit_ids

Normalized unit identifiers (reference street_unit_id), NA where a record names no unit.

name_keys

Normalized names (reference name_key). Optional, but without them an address cannot be classified: the share of records carrying the most common name is what separates a federated parent from a fiscal sponsor, and counts alone cannot.

share_min

Count above which an address, or an address + suite, counts as shared. Default 10: below that, repeats are usually variants of one organisation — an org, its foundation, its auxiliary — rather than a multi-tenant building or a sponsor's mail drop.

unit_coverage_min

Share of the records at an address that must name a suite before "several distinct suites here" is read as a fact about the building rather than about the data. Default 0.5.

Value

An np_addr_freq list: addr (records per address), addr_unit (records per address + suite), units (distinct suites per address), unit_coverage, n_names, top_name_share, class (one of "federated", "shared", "building", "cluster"), share_min and unit_coverage_min.

Details

  • One address, many distinct suites — an office building let to many nonprofits, common in cities and often a foundation's building rented out to centralize back-office services. Here the suite is the differentiator, precisely because an exact-address match surfaces every tenant as a candidate.

  • One address + suite shared by many records — a fiscal sponsor, a registered agent, or an accountant's mail drop. The suite is then evidence of nothing, and the address is worth flagging to a reviewer instead.

Feed the result to npmatch::np_compare() (addr_freq =), which annotates each pair with addr_shared, addr_units, addr_unit_shared and a reviewer-facing addr_note, and gates the suite credit in np_score(method = "hier").

See also

np_name_freq(), npmatch::np_compare()
